claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi is a high-entropy alloy suitable as the basis of the proposed material system.
CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA multilayers can be fabricated with predominantly coherent interfaces.
Increasing lattice mismatch reduces interface coherency and can produce semi-coherent and eventually incoherent interfaces.
Layer thickness and compositional gradients can be used to systematically control interface lattice mismatch in CoCrFeMnNi-based multilayers.
The degree of interface coherency is determined by the lattice mismatch between successive HEA layers.
Coherent interfaces enhance atomic diffusion along the interface.
Enhanced interface diffusion at coherent interfaces promotes diffusion-mediated creep.
Increasing lattice mismatch to create semi-coherent or incoherent interfaces disrupts interface diffusion pathways.
Semi-coherent or incoherent interfaces impede dislocation transmission more strongly than coherent interfaces.
Reduced interface coherency shifts the dominant creep mechanism from diffusion-mediated creep to dislocation-mediated creep.
CoCrFeMnNi can exhibit dislocation-associated deformation, including slip, at elevated temperatures.
A critical lattice-mismatch threshold exists beyond which the dominant creep mechanism changes.
Diffusion-controlled creep is characterized by a lower stress exponent and higher strain-rate sensitivity than the proposed dislocation-mediated regime.
The dislocation-mediated creep regime will have higher yield strength and distinct dislocation motion observable by in situ TEM.
At extremely high temperatures or very high applied stresses, diffusion- and dislocation-mediated creep may coexist.
The critical lattice-mismatch threshold may vary with alloy composition and processing parameters.
